teaches: A culture story: open on a scene with a person, a place and a year; the origin told as cause and effect; land on the turn that makes it matter now.

packet.title: How house music got its name
sentences: Around 1981 Frankie Knuckles saw a sign in a South Side Chicago bar window advertising "house music" and asked a friend what it meant.
The friend told him it was the music he played at his club, the Warehouse.
Knuckles had been the Warehouse's resident DJ since 1977, brought from New York by promoter Robert Williams.
The Warehouse's crowd was mostly Black and gay.

packet.title: From disco's collapse to a new sound
sentences: After disco collapsed commercially around 1980, labels stopped releasing new disco records.
Knuckles re-edited soul, funk, gospel and jazz records on reel-to-reel tape.
Cheap drum machines in the early 1980s added a steady four-on-the-floor beat.
Jesse Saunders and Vince Lawrence's "On and On" in 1984 is widely called the first house record.
Farley "Jackmaster" Funk's "Love Can't Turn Around" reached the British top ten in 1986.
Chicago today hosts several house music festivals every summer.
